newsitem.title: CANADA: CRTC denies CanWest Alberta application.
newsitem.headline: CRTC denies CanWest Alberta application.

text.p: The Canadian Radio-Television and Telecommunications Commission said on Friday it denied an application by CanWest Global Communications Corp for a television broadcasting license in Alberta.
The CRTC granted the license to Craig Broadcast Systems Inc, on behalf of A-Channel Inc, a private company indirectly controlled by A. Stuart Craig, a businessman from Brandon, Manitoba.

"The Commission found that the A-Channel proposals will best contribute to achieving the objectives of the Broadcasting Act," CRTC chairwoman Francoise Bertrand said in a news release. "In particular, A-Channel has proposed to broadcast more local news and other local productions, and a higher level of Canadian content during peak viewing hours."
CanWest's application had been fiercely opposed by WIC Western International Communications Ltd of Vancouver, which has four television stations in Alberta.
Analysts said CanWest, which mounted an unsuccessful takeover bid for WIC earlier this year, would have posed a major competitive threat to WIC if it had won the Alberta license.
